sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Self-Insurance Risk Underwriting for Multinational Enterprise Groups

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Republic of Panama (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax or corporate law distinctions)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid legal system rooted in Civil Law tradition with material Common Law influence in corporate, commercial, securities, and maritime matters
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama-United States Bilateral Investment Treaty and Trade Promotion Agreement
Panama-Mexico Bilateral Investment Treaty and Tax Information Exchange Agreement

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 23 of 27 April 2015 on Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism, as amended by Law No. 70 of 2019; Executive Decree No. 363 of 2015 (implementing regulations); Law No. 129 of 17 December 2020 (Legal Framework on Beneficial Ownership); Executive Decree No. 321 of 23 August 2021 and Supreme Court of Justice Agreement No. 5-2021 (operational rules of the Beneficial Ownership Register of the Registro Publico de Panama); Law No. 113 of 31 October 2017 (Special Regime for Captive Insurers and Reinsurers) together with the implementing licensing, solvency, and AML/CFT requirements of the Superintendencia de Seguros y Reaseguros de Panama (SSRP); and the binding risk-tier guidance of the Unidad de Analisis Financiero (UAF) applicable to licensed insurance-sector entities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the parent company and ultimate beneficial owner chain documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry or chamber of commerce in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Panama is a contracting state of the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; consular legalization is required only for instruments originating in non-member states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the parent company Board Resolution authorizing the formation of the captive reinsurance SPV, the proposed reinsurance business plan, and the appointment of the Panama resident agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary of the parent company, attested before a notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry or official corporate register in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copies and proof of residential address of each director, officer, and ultimate beneficial owner of the SPV, and of the proposed Panama resident agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent consulate in the country of residence of each person
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of the audited financial statements of the parent company (last three fiscal years) and a statement of solvency and available capital for the captive
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Independent external audit firm registered in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, senior management, and material counterparties of the captive SPV against: (i) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) and Consolidated Sanctions List; (ii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) the EU consolidated financial sanctions database; (iv) the domestic Panamanian PEP records maintained by the Unidad de Analisis Financiero (UAF); and (v) local judicial, insolvency, and regulatory disqualification records. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is statutorily mandated for all domestic and foreign PEPs, including verifiable source of wealth and source of funds documentation. The captive SPV must adopt a written AML/CFT manual, appoint a compliance officer resident in Panama, conduct periodic independent audits, maintain a risk-based client/counterparty acceptance policy, and file suspicious transaction reports with the UAF.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Publico de Panama - Online Search and Name Reservation module, functional through the official e-incorporation portal 'Panama Empresa' (https://www.panamaempresas.gob.pa) and the Registro Publico website (https://www.registropublico.gob.pa); the search and reservation certificate is formally denominated 'Certificado de Busqueda y Reserva de Nombre'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed corporate name must use the Latin alphabet; a Spanish-language denominacion is preferred, and any name submitted in a foreign language must be transliterated into Latin script and registered phonetically as rendered in Spanish for search indexing. The name must incorporate a corporate suffix (S.A., Corp., or Inc.) and must not be identical or phonetically identical (busqueda fonetica) to any name already inscribed in the Registro Publico de Panama.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the incorporator or resident agent must file a written administrative appeal with the Director General of the Registro Publico de Panama within 15 business days of the notification of refusal, attaching the original name search receipt and any new supporting documentation. If the rejection is grounded on phonetic identity, a revised alternative name must be proposed concurrently. The name reservation may be renewed for one additional 30-day period by paying a new statutory search fee, subject to continued availability. An adverse final decision may be challenged before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso Administrativo de la Corte Suprema de Justicia within two months of the final registry determination.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for a licensed captive reinsurance SPV. Under Law No. 113 of 2017 and the implementing regulatory framework of the Superintendencia de Seguros y Reaseguros de Panama (SSRP), the captive must maintain an operational physical office in Panama, a resident legal representative, a locally appointed compliance officer, and administrative, accounting, and underwriting records physically or electronically accessible within Panamanian territory. A virtual mailbox or a bare registered-agent address will not satisfy the licensing and substance criteria for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High - estimated 70-85% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the SSRP during the first 12 months following the issuance of the captive license; cumulative inspection probability exceeds 85% during the first full supervisory review cycle, particularly where the underwriting function, board meetings, or records are managed outside Panama without demonstrated local substance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for medium-risk-tier captive insurance SPVs in Panama

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 32 de 1927, as amended, of the Republic of Panama (General Law of Corporations), especially Articles 1-14 (formation), 15-27 (share capital), and 28-48 (directors and officers); read together with the Registry Regulations of the Registro Público de Panamá.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Mercantile Registry Division (Departamento de Registro de Personas Jurídicas)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución y Pacto Social (notarized public deed) / Articles of Incorporation filed for inscription in the Mercantile Register
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the incorporators may determine par value of at least one issued share. No escrow or capital deposit is required for incorporation. The captive reinsurance authorization separately imposes solvency capital and paid-up capital requirements established by the SSRP.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: IT IS RESOLVED: 1. That the incorporation of the Company and the subscription and issuance of its authorized shares, as stated in the Articles of Incorporation, are hereby ratified. 2. That the registered office of the Company shall be at the office of the resident agent in Panama City, Republic of Panama. 3. That [Name] is elected President, [Name] is elected Secretary, and [Name] is elected Treasurer. 4. That the President and Treasurer are authorized to open bank accounts, execute underwriting agreements, and operate SWIFT payment rails. 5. That management is directed to apply for the captive reinsurance license before the Superintendencia de Seguros y Reaseguros de Panamá. 6. That the corporate governance calendar and territorial tax treatment are approved. 7. That external auditors be appointed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Mercantile Registry, Electronic Services Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search and reservation request through the Registro Público de Panamá's electronic platform (e-Servicios) or counter, with up to three alternative names. The search will confirm availability and the reservation will be recorded for 30 business days. Pay the search and reservation tariff and retain the Certificado de Reserva de Nombre.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate names (up to three alternatives)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is unavailable or confusingly similar, select an alternative from the submitted list and reserve it; no formal appeal is required unless the refusal is contested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Panamanian Notary Public and Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Panamanian resident agent and notary to draft the Articles of Incorporation and by-laws in Spanish. The document must include the company name, registered agent, corporate purpose (captive reinsurance), term, share classes, capital structure, and governance provisions. Execute the notarial public deed or private document before a notary public.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of founders or subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or resident agent raises observations, execute a corrective supplementary instrument (aclaración) before inscription; no material defect remains after correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Sociedad Anónima in the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Mercantile Registry Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Articles of Incorporation with the Mercantile Registry of the Registro Público. Pay the registration fee. Upon examination, the Registrar issues a certificate of inscription with registration number and corporate file (ficha), which perfects the corporate personality.
required_dossiers: Notarized power of attorney, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a razón de no inscribir is issued, submit requested corrections or additional documentation within ten business days; a registral appeal is available if the refusal is contested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution, Share Issuance, and Officer Appointment Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Mercantile Registry Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of directors, adopt the first board resolution, issue share certificates, and record appointment of officers. File the Certificate of Appointment of Directors and Officers with the Public Registry and update the corporate ledger with share subscription and beneficial ownership information where required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct spelling or order of officers by supplemental board resolution and re-file; late filing penalties can be cured by payment and correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Identification (RUC) and Municipal Operating Permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance; Municipality of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation with the DGI for tax identification (RUC) using the electronic tax platform. After obtaining the RUC, apply for the municipal Aviso de Operación and business license with the relevant municipality. The municipality verifies the registered office address and issues the operating permit.
required_dossiers: Proof of office address and lease
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUC or municipal application is queried, provide the missing lease or title evidence and correct administrative data; use the municipal adjustment or correction process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Captive Reinsurer License Application before SSRP
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Superintendencia de Seguros y Reaseguros de Panamá (SSRP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the captive reinsurer license request to the SSRP after incorporation and RUC issuance. Provide the business plan, corporate governance and risk management policies, solvency capital projection, AML/CFT program, captive reinsurance program covering parent-company risks, and proof of paid-up capital according to SSRP regulations. The SSRP reviews the dossier and, once satisfied, grants the captive reinsurer license.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the SSRP's observations within 15 business days; amend the application and resubmit with additional documentation as required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Superintendencia de Seguros y Reaseguros de Panamá (SSRP)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia para Reaseguradora Cautiva (Captive Reinsurer Operating License)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Category I registration for office-based insurance operations; no full EIA required unless a separate physical underwriting or processing facility is opened
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For pure office captive operations: no industrial VOC discharge; domestic wastewater must comply with municipal sewer standards; any standby generator requires MiAMBIENTE registration for emission testing; battery and electronic waste disposed through certified handlers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the Dirección General de Bomberos de Panamá; municipal occupancy and structural-load statement from the office landlord; occupational health and hygiene clearance from the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; electronic portal: e-Tax (https://etax.mef.gob.pa)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned captive reinsurer must: (1) appoint a Panamanian resident agent; (2) incorporate a Sociedad Anónima by notarized public deed and register it in the Registro Público; (3) obtain the Aviso de Operación and register in the DGI to receive the Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC); (4) activate the ITBMS and withholding-tax accounts in the e-Tax portal using an authorized digital-signature credential; (5) obtain the captive reinsurance license from the Superintendencia de Seguros y Reaseguros de Panamá before commencing underwriting. DGI issues the RUC upon submission of the public deed, resident-agent certificate, Articles of Incorporation, and proof of license application; the RUC is mandatory for issuing any invoice or receiving taxable premiums.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama has no check-the-box election and no hybrid-mismatch entity election; the Sociedad Anónima is a separate taxable entity, not a pass-through. Territorial taxation is mandatory: only Panama-source income is subject to corporate income tax (ISR), while overseas-risk reinsurance income is outside the Panamanian net. Options through advance tax rulings include the accounting basis for technical reserves and deductibility of captive reinsurance commission; there is no free election to change entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general ITBMS registration threshold; all legal entities engaged in taxable supplies of goods or services in Panama must register. Only natural persons with annual gross income up to B/.36,000 (USD/PAB) may use the simplified small-taxpayer regime; corporate captive reinsurers cannot use it.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing under the DGI's Facturación Electrónica de Panamá: invoices must be transmitted through DGI-authorized software to the e-Tax API, validated in real time, and issued only after receiving a unique Código de Autorización (UAC) and QR code. The API supports SOAP/REST clearance with mutual TLS and digital certificates; paper/fiscal-printer fallback is allowed only during transition or for non-digitized taxpayers, not for a licensed reinsurer.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are zero-rated if sold by a Panamanian exporter to a non-resident, physically leave Panama under customs control, transfer title to the foreign buyer, and the price is paid by the foreign buyer. Services are zero-rated (or outside the ITBMS base) if supplied to a non-resident for use wholly outside Panama; for captive reinsurance, the relevant test is that no insured risk is located in Panama, the reinsured is a foreign licensed insurer/group captive, and the underwriting and risk management are carried out abroad. Input ITBMS attributable to zero-rated exports can be credited or refunded through DGI returns.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUCA / Boleta de Exportación) validated by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill issued by an independent carrier evidencing physical exit from Panama
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT credit confirmation from the Panamanian bank evidencing receipt of the export consideration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI verification programs cross-match customs declarations, bank receipts, and ITBMS returns. Unsupported or simulated zero-rated exports are reclassified as taxable at 7% with legal interest (approximately 1.5% per month); fines range from 100% to 500% of the omitted tax, and false documentation can trigger criminal tax-fraud charges, suspension or cancellation of the RUC, and retroactive reassessments for up to five years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) as the primary banking and AML/CFT supervisory authority; Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent of the Republic of Panama, but Panama has no formal central bank or foreign-exchange administration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is a fully dollarized economy; the US dollar is legal tender under Cabinet Decree No. 238 of 1904. There is no exchange-control regime and no legal distinction between current and capital account transactions for convertibility purposes. Profit remittances and capital repatriation are freely permitted without central-bank approval, subject only to banking-sector source-of-funds validation, the captive's statutory licensing obligations under the Superintendencia de Seguros y Reaseguros de Panamá (SSRP), and compliance with the Money Laundering Prevention Act (Law 42/2014).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender rule or mandatory conversion ratio applies. Panama imposes no export-proceeds surrender or repatriation timeline; a captive reinsurance SPV may retain US-dollar receipts in any SBP-licensed bank without conversion requirements.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMI passports are not recognized in Panama. Under Law 124 of 2020, a locally licensed 'empresa de dinero electrónico' (EDE) is permitted to provide payment and e-money services, but such entities lack full banking powers and cannot hold or safeguard reinsurance trust assets, statutory capital escrow balances, or captive reserves. The SBP does not authorize offshore EMIs to operate a deposit-taking or clearing account for a Panamanian S.A. without a branch or subsidiary license; for this captive reinsurance SPV, a licensed commercial bank must serve as the clearing and custody counterparty.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly created Sociedad Anónima, the SBP-compliant corporate opening process generally requires physical or bank-confirmed video identity verification of the ultimate beneficial owner, directors, and signatories. Purely remote onboarding is rarely granted; most tier-1 banks require at least a notarized in-country submission through the registered agent, original or apostilled powers of attorney, and a virtual interview with a compliance officer. If international directors are appointed, the bank will typically insist on a face-to-face interview at the bank's offices or at a Panamanian embassy, unless the bank approves an enhanced remote KYC protocol.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly formed Panama S.A. with historical bearer-share flexibility, nominee directors, and insufficient local substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cancelled or certified registered share ledger evidencing no outstanding bearer shares, SBP beneficial ownership declarations, sworn passports, director CVs and tax ID, a Panamanian registered-agent attestation, board resolutions demonstrating the captive's held-in-trust purpose, audited financial statements or opening balance sheet, and an AML/KYC policy manual aligned with Law 42/2014.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Reinsurance contributions or capital injections sourced from FATF grey-listed jurisdictions or complex multi-tier group structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group consolidated financial statements, audit trail of the remitting entities, certificates of tax residency, transfer pricing documentation, intercompany reinsurance agreements, source-of-wealth statements for all ultimate beneficial owners, sanctions screening results, and a compliance-committee sign-off evidencing the direct link between the premium flow and the captive's active underwriting portfolio.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected high-velocity US-dollar transactions or cross-border movement outside the approved treasury plan.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Actuarial reserve certificate issued by a qualified actuary, reinsurance treaty schedule, segregated portfolio statement, board-approved treasury and investment policy, SWIFT MT103 transaction samples, SSRP statutory declaration, and a detailed variance report reconciling all inflows with ceded premiums and reserve obligations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections must be routed by SWIFT MT103 from the ultimate controlling company to the captive's operational or capital escrow account at an SBP-licensed Panamanian bank. Because Panama has no exchange control, no central-bank authorization is required; however, to support KYC and AML reviews, the SWIFT field must state 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION / PAID-IN CAPITAL – LICENSED CAPTIVE REINSURANCE SPV' and should be accompanied by a board resolution, notarized capital subscription agreement, and source-of-funds evidence. The receiving bank will verify the intended purpose code, the beneficial owner against sanctions lists, and the consistency of the remittance name with the corporate KYC file; disbursement to the operational account is permitted only after the funds are cleared and the bank's enhanced due diligence is satisfied.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for reinsurance settlements, retrocession premiums, fronting commissions, and brokerage fees should be executed via SWIFT MT103 (customer transfer) or SWIFT MT202 COV (interbank reimbursement) with final settlement in US dollars through the bank's US correspondent (typically located in New York or Florida). For treaty documentation requiring a documentary mechanism, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit or a standby LC may be used as a collateral vehicle under an ISDA/ICMA framework. Freedom-of-payment is unrestricted, but each transfer must carry a consistent narrative referencing the captive's treaty number, claim reference, and policy schedule to satisfy the SSRP and SBP transaction-monitoring obligations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla over-the-counter (OTC) USD-forward contracts with an SBP-licensed bank or an international bank under an ISDA Master Agreement; no prior government authorization is required.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in Latin American currencies (e.g., USD/MXN, USD/BRL, USD/COP) used to hedge fronting or retrocession exposures denominated in foreign currency; permitted to the extent they mirror the captive's actual treaty obligations.

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) between USD and a foreign currency for net investment positions or foreign-ceded portfolio liabilities, permitted under Panamanian law when documented through an SBP-regulated counterparty and supported by a board-approved derivative authorization.

Currency options and plain collars on a non-speculative basis; subject to the captive's statutory investment rules and the SBP requirement that the hedge must be economically related to a specific reinsurance contract or reserve currency exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Franchise Tax (Tasa Única Anual)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (Panama Revenue Authority, DGI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before July 31 of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a 10% statutory surcharge plus monthly interest; persistent non-payment produces a delinquency certificate and eventual administrative suspension or strike-off at the Panamanian Public Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración Anual de Impuesto sobre la Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year end, no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monetary fines up to USD 10,000, accrued interest on unreported tax, and potential tax liens or seizure proceedings for continued non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Declaration (Declaración Anual de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI through the registered agent; records are electronically registered under the beneficial ownership regime (Law 23 of 2017)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary of incorporation; any change in beneficial ownership must be updated within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines per Law 23 of 2017, potentially up to USD 250,000, together with suspension of corporate rights and refusal of notarial or registry services.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Licensed Captive Reinsurance Annual Report and Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the end of the fiscal year, or by April 30 for calendar-year entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties up to USD 50,000, possible suspension of underwriting operations, and ultimate revocation of the captive reinsurance license for repeat violation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies to all licensed captive reinsurance companies without revenue or asset exemption. Non-regulated Sociedades Anónimas in Panama generally require an audited financial statement when exceeding DGI-prescribed size thresholds, typically based on total assets and gross annual income.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted by the Superintendencia de Seguros y Reaseguradoras for insurance and reinsurance entities; tax basis for the DGI uses Panama's territorial income tax rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each Sociedad Anónima must annually confirm current beneficial ownership information to its registered agent within 30 days of the anniversary of incorporation. The confirmation must be repeated upon any change in ownership; the registered agent maintains the Beneficial Ownership Register and files mandatory data with the DGI where required.
